claims.text: Benztropine for extrapyramidal disorders due to neuroleptics: 1 to 4 mg once or twice a day orally, individualized;
claims.quote: In treating extrapyramidal disorders due to neuroleptic drugs (e.g., phenothiazines), the recommended dosage is 1 to 4 mg once or twice a day orally. Dosage must be individualized according to the need of the patient.

claims.text: when they develop soon after starting the neuroleptic (likely transient), one to 2 mg two or three times a day usually gives relief within one or two days; after one or two weeks withdraw it to see if it's still needed.
claims.quote: When extrapyramidal disorders develop soon after initiation of treatment with neuroleptic drugs (e.g., phenothiazines), they are likely to be transient. One to 2 mg of benztropine mesylate tablets two or three times a day usually provides relief within one or two days. After one or two weeks the drug should be withdrawn to determine the continued need for it.

claims.text: Not recommended in tardive dyskinesia: antiparkinsonism agents don't relieve it and in some instances may aggravate it.
claims.quote: Antiparkinsonism agents do not alleviate the symptoms of tardive dyskinesia, and in some instances may aggravate them. Benztropine mesylate is not recommended for use in patients with tardive dyskinesia.

claims.text: Benztropine may cause anhidrosis: use caution in hot weather, especially with other atropine-like drugs or manual labor in heat.
claims.quote: it may produce anhidrosis. For this reason, it should be administered with caution during hot weather, especially when given concomitantly with other atropine-like drugs to the chronically ill, the alcoholic, those who have central nervous system disease, and those who do manual labor in a hot environment.

claims.text: With phenothiazines, haloperidol or other anticholinergic or antidopaminergic drugs, report GI complaints, fever or heat intolerance promptly (paralytic ileus, hyperthermia and heat stroke have sometimes been fatal).
claims.quote: When benztropine mesylate is given concomitantly with phenothiazines, haloperidol, or other drugs with anticholinergic or antidopaminergic activity, patients should be advised to report gastrointestinal complaints, fever or heat intolerance promptly. Paralytic ileus, hyperthermia and heat stroke, all of which have sometimes been fatal

claims.text: Anticholinergic intoxication: physostigmine 1 to 2 mg SC or IV reportedly reverses symptoms; otherwise treatment is symptomatic and supportive.
claims.quote: Physostigmine salicylate, 1 to 2 mg, SC or IV, reportedly will reverse symptoms of anticholinergic intoxication. * A second injection may be given after 2 hours if required. Otherwise treatment is symptomatic and supportive.
